summary: Two potentially material gaps were tested skeptically: hidden conditionality in the two-star residual degree ceilings, and insufficient justification of the singleton-trace cap used by the Profile A completion count. The explicit two-star wrapper discharges its degree assumptions without I(27), and the new trace explanation matches the inherited lemma including injective deletion and distinct sunflower members. Neither objection survives the inspected evidence.

checks.scope: Could the unconditional two-star bound conceal I(27) in the residual degree assumption?
checks.method: Inspected independent_twenty_stars_card_le_eighty in TwoHighEighty.lean, following its construction of the exact high-point set and the degree-at-most-nineteen obligation.
checks.observation: The wrapper puts distinct x,y into highPoints and applies the inherited bound high_points_card_le_two with only uniformity and sunflower-freeness. Every other point has degree at most twenty by the unconditional rank-three link bound and cannot have degree twenty because highPoints={x,y}; integrality gives nineteen. The internal residual caps 14 and 9 therefore do not import an unstated boundary hypothesis, support bound or I(27).

checks.scope: Could the repaired singleton-trace explanation fail to deliver cap ten or the +2 meeting excess?
checks.method: Matched the revised Section 4 sentence to Erdos20RankFour.singleton_trace_card_le_ten and singleton_intersection_card_le_forty; reconstructed deletion, distinctness and anchor counting.
checks.observation: A row with exact trace {v} on R differs from R because R has four points. Deleting v is injective and gives sunflower-free triples outside R. Two disjoint distinct residues would lift to two rows meeting each other and R exactly in {v}, yielding three distinct sunflower members; hence the residues are intersecting and the inherited cap ten applies. There are four possible v, giving total singleton mass at most forty. The closed neighborhood includes R, which contributes four rather than two incidences, so the +2 excess is retained. The repair addresses the committed explanatory gap.
